questions.text: In the diamonds log-log model, the slope for log(carat) is approximately 1.68. This means:
options: A 1-carat increase in weight increases price by $1.68
A 1% increase in carat is associated with approximately a 1.68% increase in price (a power law)
Each carat multiplies the price by 1.68
68% of the variance in price is explained by carat weight
questions.explanation: On a log-log scale, the slope is a power-law exponent. slope = 1.68 means price scales as carat^1.68 — a 1% increase in carat → 1.68% increase in price.

questions.text: In the flights many-models analysis, R² < 0.05 for all carriers. This means:
options: Time of day and month explain less than 5% of the variance in departure delays
Departure delays do not vary by hour or month
questions.explanation: R² measures the fraction of variance explained. R² = 0.05 means 95% of the variance in delays is unexplained by hour + month — weather, knock-on delays, and other factors dominate.

questions.text: nls() can always find the optimal parameters regardless of the starting values provided.
questions.explanation: nls() uses an iterative algorithm that can fail to converge or get stuck if starting values are far from the true parameters. Good starting values from domain knowledge or a coarse grid search are essential.

questions.text: broom::tidy() applied to an lm() object returns:
options: A single row with model-level statistics (R², AIC, df)
A data frame with one row per coefficient: term, estimate, std.error, statistic, p.value
The fitted values for each observation
questions.explanation: broom::tidy() converts model objects into a tidy data frame with one row per term (coefficient). This makes it easy to compare coefficients across many models using dplyr operations.

questions.text: In the diamonds case study, diamonds with large POSITIVE residuals from the log-log model tend to have what characteristic?
options: Poor quality attributes: Fair cut, tinted colour, low clarity
Exceptional quality: Ideal cut, colourless colour, high clarity
They are duplicated observations in the dataset
questions.explanation: A positive residual means actual price >> carat-predicted price. Diamonds that command a premium relative to their weight are those with exceptional quality (Ideal cut, D/E colour, IF/VVS clarity). The simple model underestimates their price because it ignores quality.
